Captain Fromm and his skeleton crew have amassed a massive treasure, and now is your chance to take it all. Players take on the role of Pirates who are boarding Skelit's Revenge for one purpose....to take the loot. They must battle the flames, the skeleton crew, and their own fatigue if they hope to make it out alive. Dead Men Tell No Tales is a co-operative game for 1-5 players. The game uses the common Action Point system to determine what a player does on their turn...with a twist. As players work together, they can pass their Actions on to their teammates in order to best utilize the assets that they have. Players will build the board as they play, ensuring that no two games will ever be alike. As they search the ship for the Treasure, they will encounter Enemies and Guards that they must battle, along with various items that will help them in their quest. all the while, battling the inferno that resulted when they took over the ship. Unique systems for tracking fire, enemy movement, and a player’s fatigue all combine into an interesting and unique cooperative gaming experience. Do you and your crew have what it takes to make off with all of the treasure and live to tell the story? Or are you going down with the ship in Dead Men Tell No Tales? [Rating: 2/10] Pirate themed firefighters... nuff said.  Feels like a rethemed version of Forbidden Desert, but with crappy dice instead of tiles.  Feels like an endless game of whack-a-mole.

[Rating: 2/10] exactly the kind of thing I fuckin hate: having to track 7 or 8 variables on each move just so they can fluctuate back and forth.

[Rating: 2/10] #Coop  Unfortunately not very thematic. I felt more like a firefighter than a pirate. And turning dice isn't very entertaining. And nothing entertaining is happening during the entire game. A game that you easily can play by your own. [Rating: 3/10] I did not care for this game at all.  Very challenging co-op, on the lvl with Ghost Stories or Pandemic on harder settings.

[Rating: 3/10] No cats nor dogs popping just pass you here but tile placement, exploration, dice rolling and looting trying to prevent explosions, overruns, fatigue and spreading skeletons. DMTNT is a bag of escalating loosing conditions slowly but surely putting you in unwinnable situations. Because difficulty is decided by random dice, random tiles, random tokens and random cards all having immediate effects with no clues of whatever's coming, there is more to do but nothing to solve in this coop.

[Rating: 3/10] Incredibly bland cooperative game where luck seems to determine the difficulty of the game. The most exciting part was putting the game away. Traded away.

[Rating: 3/10] Have you ever played 'Pandemic', and thought "Man, what this game really needs is about 3 more types of things to track, a meaningless tile-laying mechanic, and maybe a game could take more than twice as long to play? Oh, and pirates, because everything is better with pirates!" Well, here's the game for you! It's...uhhh...'pointlessly complicated' would be a good description.

[Rating: 3/10] A Pandemic spinoff about firefighters that sometimes dress up as pirates and fight diseases on a ship. This is a good start to a prototype about firefighters that needs a lot more work to be interesting. Components are amazing, but I've seen all this mechanism before a couple of times executed much cleaner. I don't understand who the target for this game is? Is it supposed to be heavy puzzle co-op? It isn't. A gateway? Not at all. A climatic game? With all these firefighting? I'm very sorry but this adds nothing new to the crowded genre, that desperatly needs some innovation.

[Rating: 3/10] I like games that utilize random set up or procedural generation. This game has that by the tiles emerging in a random order. That being said, the randomness made it feel more frustrating than fun when trying to solve the puzzle. Also the fire spreading ramps up so quickly I never felt like I had a handle on anything at any point during the game.

[Rating: 3/10] Tried this on BGA. Couldn't get into it, found it incredibly boring, and couldn't even determine what was worth doing to help manage all the threats, other than fighting deckhands and fires constantly. Seemed too close to a Pandemic style game to my liking.

[Rating: 3.5/10] [thing=141423][/thing] has some interesting mechanics - the fatigue track, the actions against the fire and how it works; but, the end result of everything put together is a game to drop dead of boredom: in the game I was in no one was having fun nor there was excitement, as even the event cards are lame: just enemies that enter/move and the chance of increasing fire. These could be exciting, but aren't.  Play lasted for around 90 minutes, but felt like 180.
